title: Meal planner architecture
subtitle: For you and anyone who builds the app: how the Flutter app, the bundled catalog and Firebase fit together.
tldr: Seven slides with the architecture diagrams from ARCHITECTURE.md: system context, layers, a data flow, the data model, auth, and next steps. Two picks: framework and theme.

sections.title: Brief
sections.lead: You present it yourself, to collaborators or reviewers, in about 10 minutes.

blocks.md:
**Audience:** a Flutter developer joining the project, or a reviewer checking the design before Setup starts. They see it on a laptop screen or a shared call.

**Story:** context → layers → one request end to end → data model → auth → next steps.

Every diagram is drawn from the current [ARCHITECTURE.md](../../ARCHITECTURE.md). Nothing here is built or measured yet.

items.text: Which framework do the slides use?
items.sub: Recommend the plain kit: its slide classes ship with bluedoc, so the deck needs nothing installed.

choices.label: Plain kit
choices.md: Slide classes that ship with bluedoc: titles, columns, big numbers. The deck needs nothing installed and exports as one file.

choices.label: HorizonUI
choices.md: HorizonUI's cards, tables and charts on the slides. Closer to a product dashboard; the slides take longer to lay out.

items.sub: Recommend Light: the diagrams use thin borders and muted labels, which read best on a light background.

choices.label: Light
choices.md: Suits a laptop screen, a screen share, or a PDF you print. Thin borders and grey labels stay legible.

choices.label: Dark
choices.md: Suits a projector in a dark room. Muted labels lose some contrast, so small text on the data-model slide gets harder to read.

sections.title: Slides
sections.lead: Seven slides, played top to bottom: title, context, layers, flow, data, auth, next steps.

artboards.title: Title: a Flutter app that talks straight to Firebase
artboards.notes: The whole system in one line: there is no backend we write. Three ideas carry the design: Firebase is the backend, the recipe catalog ships inside the app, and Firestore's offline cache is the sync layer.

artboards.title: System context: phone and Firebase services
artboards.notes: Left: the app holds the catalog, the search index and Firestore's offline cache. Right: the four Firebase services we use through V1. Analytics only collects after consent. Storage, FCM, Remote Config and Functions wait for V2.

artboards.title: Layers: dependencies point inward
artboards.notes: One package, layers as folders. Features depend on domain and design_system. Data and handlers implement ports declared in domain, so domain never imports data or a Firebase SDK. Only the app layer touches GetIt.

artboards.title: Data flow: mark lunch eaten
artboards.notes: Walk the arrow left to right. The key point is the return path: the snapshot stream fires from the local cache, so the UI is instant even offline. We never await the write, because with persistence on it only completes when the server acknowledges. Analytics is logged in the use case.

artboards.title: Data model: catalog in the app, user data in Firestore
artboards.notes: Catalog: bundled JSON, with updates pulled by updatedAt and tombstones for deletions. User data: one day record per date is the plan, the tracker and history. Items carry name snapshots so catalog edits never rewrite history. Shopping lines are a map: derived keys d_ingredient_unit, manual keys m_.

artboards.title: Auth: guest first, link keeps the UID
artboards.notes: Anonymous on first launch, link Google or Apple to the same UID. If the provider already owns another account, show an explicit dialog; never merge silently. Deletion order matters: re-auth, revoke Apple token, delete data while signed in, then delete the Auth user.

artboards.title: Next: build Setup S1–S3 on this shape
artboards.notes: Setup is the next milestone in WORKPLAN.md. The Firestore location is permanent, so pick asia-south1 once. Content work starts now, alongside engineering.
